config.title: Pagination

intro.title: Pagination
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple pagination component for a list of items in a Vue application. You will learn how to split a large dataset into smaller, manageable pages that users can navigate through. The core programming concepts involved are reactive state management to track the current page and computed properties to calculate which items to display. You will use Vue's ref for state, computed for derived data, and template syntax to render the page controls. By the end, you will have a functional pagination system that responds to user clicks.
intro.usecase: Pagination is essential for managing large datasets in real-world applications like e-commerce product listings, search engine results, and content management dashboards. Developers implement pagination controls to break extensive data into manageable pages, improving performance and user experience. You'll find pagination in social media feeds, admin panels displaying user records, and any interface where data needs to be browsed efficiently without overwhelming the user or the browser.

objectives: Implement a reactive data property to store pagination state (current page, items per page, total items)
Construct computed properties to calculate total pages and visible page range
Apply conditional rendering to display pagination controls only when needed
Bind click handlers to pagination buttons that update the current page
Configure a method to fetch and display paginated data based on current page
Integrate pagination controls with a data table or list component
Manulate the pagination UI to highlight the active page and disable irrelevant buttons
